questions.question: What is a volcanogenic massive sulphide (VMS) deposit?

facts: it forms from hydrothermal fluids venting at or just below the seafloor in submarine volcanic settings
it is a stratiform lens of massive sulphides (pyrite, chalcopyrite, sphalerite, galena) often with a footwall stockwork
it is mined for copper, zinc, lead, and often gold and silver
truth.tolerance: the key points must be present and correct; extra correct detail is fine
truth.source: general knowledge, written before any system was asked

questions.question: What is a strip ratio in open-pit mining?

facts: the ratio of waste rock removed to ore mined (for example tonnes of waste per tonne of ore)
a higher strip ratio raises mining cost per tonne of ore and lowers the economic pit limit
it can vary through the life of a pit and is used in pit optimisation and mine planning
truth.tolerance: the key points must be present and correct; extra correct detail is fine
truth.source: general knowledge, written before any system was asked
